resolved.blocks: R1 pristine-source guarantee for any externalsrc recipe with BBCLASSEXTEND
resolved.description: BBCLASSEXTEND = "native" on an externalsrc recipe gives the target and native variants the SAME EXTERNALSRC source tree, and bitbake schedules them concurrently. Isolated empirically: `bitbake -c compile -f symoneural-numpy-native` alone leaves the tree clean (mode 775), `-f symoneural-numpy` alone leaves it clean, but a full build that runs both flips numpy/_core/src/umath/loops_hyperbolic.dispatch.cpp.src from 100755 to 100644. Content is unchanged; the exec bit is lost because a writer rewrites the file. Options: drop BBCLASSEXTEND on externalsrc recipes, serialise the two, or give the native variant its own tree. Not resolved tonight.
resolved.resolution: RESOLVED by Phase 10b. symoneural-pristine.bbclass gives EVERY recipe variant its own disposable export (git archive HEAD -> ${WORKDIR}/pristine), so the target and native variants no longer share a tree. This is option 3 from the original description, applied universally rather than per recipe. Evidence: 41/41 acquired trees reported clean under `git status --porcelain --ignored=traditional` DURING a live build that scheduled both symoneural-numpy and symoneural-numpy-native; 0 dirty, 0 ignored residue. The negative test (tree moved off its pin) failed correctly with the PIN MISMATCH fatal.

resolved.description: No component demonstrated to compile with no network after bitbake -c fetch. Enumeration is not proof.
resolved.resolution: PROVEN UNDER EXTERNALSRC ONLY - not yet reproduced under symoneural-pristine. Phase 5, symoneural-stratum: `--runall=fetch` rc=0, then `BB_NO_NETWORK=1 bitbake symoneural-stratum` -> do_compile Succeeded, 0 NetworkAccess denials, 102 rlibs, across rust 1.98.1 + LLVM 23 + 233 crate:// entries. That run predates symoneural-pristine. The class as first written set do_fetch[noexec]=1, which silently prevented the crate:// closure from being fetched at all (empty sources/cargo_home/bitbake; stratum failed with 'no matching package named bitcoin'). Fixed by stripping only the upstream git:// URI at parse time and letting do_fetch run. RE-PROOF REQUIRED under the class before any release claim - do not cite the Phase 5 numbers as current.

resolved.description: symoneural-stratum-crates.inc declared 233 crate:// entries against a 177-package Cargo.lock, including bitcoin/0.32.100 alongside 0.32.8. Raised as a possible stale or mis-derived closure.
resolved.resolution: RESOLVED by N5. The committed symoneural-stratum-crates.inc is AUTHORITATIVE: regenerating it with `bitbake -c update_crates` from the pristine export at SRCREV produced a BYTE-IDENTICAL file (233 == 233, diff -q clean), so the closure is reproducible from the pin. The apparent 233-vs-177 discrepancy was never a pin-integrity problem. The tree carries TWO lockfiles - root Cargo.lock (177 packages) and fuzz/Cargo.lock (87) - whose union is 202 distinct (name, version) pairs, and cargo-update-recipe-crates correctly covers both. Entries in the .inc present in NEITHER lockfile: 0. The bitcoin/0.32.100, bitcoin-io/0.1.100, bitcoin-units/0.1.100 and base58ck/0.1.100 entries that looked like phantoms are real crates.io releases reached via the fuzz lockfile (both 0.32.8 and 0.32.100 fetched successfully). The 17 lockfile packages with NO crate:// entry are the workspace's own path members - stratum-core plus the 16 SV2 libraries - which are built from source, not fetched. NOTE: including the fuzz lockfile pulls crates the production build does not link. Correct, but larger than strictly needed.

resolved.description: Not acquired. Release decision specifies v2 GA 2.0.0 at cc4b41617ce3601b1290d67216ea0b194a3cd9ac; tag-to-commit unverified and mixed MIT / Apache-2.0 / CC-BY-4.0 treatment uncharacterised.
resolved.resolution: REFERENCE-ONLY by rule (Advisor E2). Acquired and pinned at cc4b41617ce3601b1290d67216ea0b194a3cd9ac; NOT built from source. Reason recorded verbatim: "pnpm catalog: protocol unsupported by npm / OE npm class". Evidence: `npm error code EUNSUPPORTEDPROTOCOL / Unsupported URL Type "catalog:": catalog:runtimeShared`. resolved.description: pydantic requires pydantic-core (Rust/maturin). meta-python supplies python3-pydantic-core 2.46.4 and it is BORROWED tonight so the API stack can build. But D2's rule is 'own what you ship, borrow what you only build with', and pydantic-core is linked into the shipped runtime, not merely used to build it. Under D2 it should be SyMoNeuRaL-owned, which means acquiring it as a source component. Recorded, not decided.
resolved.resolution: REVERSES the earlier borrow ruling. Decision: **OWN** it. "Own what you ship" applies here because pydantic-core is a RUNTIME dependency of pydantic, and Symoneural-API SHIPS pydantic. Without it `import pydantic` fails at runtime and 11e cannot start - borrowing python3-pydantic-core from meta-python would have put a component we ship outside our own pin. ACTION: acquire pydantic/pydantic-core under A7 IN PHASE 11, at the version pydantic's own tag pins: core-v2.46.5. inherit python_maturin; crate closure tracked in a .inc like symoneural-stratum's. NOTE the convergence: core-v2.46.5 and v2.13.5 both point at pydantic's SRCREV 001dea020e0809844e5b17666432c9135a976f46. Per E4 PV follows the package the recipe builds, so symoneural-pydantic correctly took 2.13.5 and NOT core-v2.46.5 - and the tag set aside then is precisely the pin this acquisition needs.

resolved.description: scipy requires a Fortran compiler. The OE cross toolchain is built LANGUAGES="c,c++" with FORTRAN="", so x86_64-oe-linux-gfortran does not exist. Evidence: scipy meson.build:91 'Unknown compiler(s): x86_64-oe-linux-gfortran', log tmp/work/x86-64-v3-oe-linux/symoneural-scipy/1.18.1/temp/log.do_compile.2878019. TOOLCHAIN decision, not a recipe fix: either rebuild gcc-cross with fortran enabled (FORTRAN:forcevariable = ",fortran"), or accept scipy/scikit-learn as unbuildable on this toolchain. Not resolvable by guessing.
resolved.resolution: RESOLVED by rule (Advisor O4): Fortran enabled ESTATE-WIDE in 10a. symoneural.conf carries FORTRAN:forcevariable = ",fortran" and RUNTIMETARGET:append:pn-gcc-runtime = " libquadmath"; the cross toolchain built rc=0 in ~10 min and 2.4 GB / 255 sstate entries were rsync'd per R10. Corroborated by symoneural-openblas, which links LAPACK with 2304 Fortran-mangled symbols (dgesvd_, dsyev_, dgetrf_, dpotrf_). The original description framed this as a TOOLCHAIN decision - rebuild gcc-cross with fortran, or accept scipy/scikit-learn as unbuildable. The first was taken. Conditionally closed: the toolchain exists and the decision is made, but it CLOSES FOR REAL when 11b actually builds scipy and scikit-learn with it. Until then the toolchain is proven, the consumer is not.

resolved.description: Phase 11's 11b DEPENDS list names python3-pythran-native. VERIFIED ABSENT: `find ~/symoneural-bootstrap-master -iname '*pythran*'` returns NOTHING - no pythran recipe exists in openembedded-core, meta-oe or meta-python. Its own hard dependency python3-beniget is ALSO absent (gast and ply are present). As written, 11b fails at parse with "Nothing PROVIDES python3-pythran-native".
resolved.resolution: DECIDED: path (A) - disable pythran at build. Not held open further; both paths were recorded, the absence was verified three ways (no *pythran* file anywhere in the bootstrap; python3-beniget absent; gast and ply present), and the default was stated. pythran is OPTIONAL upstream, so scipy builds without it at some cost to hot-loop optimisation. ACTION for 11b: keep -Duse-pythran=false (already present in symoneural-scipy as EXTRA_OEMESON) and record 'pythran: not acquired, disabled at build'. DROP python3-pythran-native from 11b's DEPENDS - as written that line fails at parse with 'Nothing PROVIDES python3-pythran-native'. REVERSIBLE: if Garrett wants pythran, path (B) acquires pythran AND beniget under A7. Nothing here forecloses that.

resolved.blocks: Symoneural-CLI build scope; target nodejs in the estate
resolved.description: Hand-authored recipe built rc=0 with 0 errors, proving the npmsw approach works. But nothing consumes it, and building it forces a Node runtime onto the target via npm.bbclass:27 RDEPENDS:${PN}:append:class-target = " nodejs".
resolved.resolution: REFERENCE-ONLY by ruling. Tree stays ACQUIRED and PINNED at 135f71e9297683e14614d4307081c0273ed0a09c; the recipe retires. EVIDENCE: no DEPENDS or RDEPENDS anywhere names it - the only recipe hits are its own HOMEPAGE and SYMON_TREE, and the single phase-spec hit (phase-15-report.md:113) is incidental prose, not a consumer. CLI's actual client is symoneural-anthropic-sdk-python, built clean at 2817 files. Same rule already applied to mcp typescript-sdk and workers-sdk. CONSEQUENCE: with hls.js dropping target nodejs (RDEPENDS:${PN}:remove), TARGET NODEJS IS REQUIRED BY NOTHING and never enters a shipped image. nodejs-native stays - it is what builds the hls.js bundle. COST ALREADY PAID AND CACHED: target nodejs 9.1 GB / ~1 h, nodejs-native 1.6 GB / ~30 min, both in sstate. Not wasted - the build proved the hand-authored recipe is correct, and sstate makes any future need free.

resolved.description: The prior run built THREE models that are not in acquisition/model-register.json: symon-1.0-32b-q2_k_xl (12,797,352,608 B, unsloth/Qwen3-32B-GGUF), symon-1.0-30b-a3b-q2_k_l (11,331,539,360 B, unsloth/Qwen3-30B-A3B-Instruct-2507-GGUF), and symon-openai-20b (openai/gpt-oss-20b). Recovered from Claude history 2026-09-11; they exist in no other record and are not on disk.
resolved.resolution: DECIDED (DECISIONS.md §4). DROP Qwen3-32B (11.9 GB) and Qwen3-30B-A3B (10.6 GB): no gate consumes them, and a register listing models nothing uses is the same defect class as a LIC_FILES_CHKSUM naming an absent path. ACQUIRE gpt-oss-20b, register it with sha256, but DO NOT REBRAND and DO NOT DEFAULT it. Evidence from this estate's own history: it needs ~12.8 GiB against 7.1 GiB free with Qwen holding 8.3 GiB, so on a 16 GB card it EVICTS chat rather than joining it; the benchmark that would justify it was not base-vs-base (Qwen ran on the production engine with adapter, draft model and -c 65536 -np 2, gpt-oss ran bare on -ngl 99 -c 8192); it carries its own LICENSE and USAGE_POLICY rather than Apache-2.0; and its reasoning_effort control was never varied. Phase 16b settles it by fair measurement.

resolved.blocks: Common (torch CUDA), LLM (llama sm_120), Crypto (kawpowminer), Tune (CuPy/cuda-python), Diffuse
resolved.resolution: ONE CUDA authority: the estate's binary toolkit recipe (Phase 12 S1) at 13.4.1 - the generation the host driver 615.71.09 runs, the host toolkit is installed at (/usr/local/cuda-13.4, nvrtc 13.4.59), and cuda-python is pinned to (v13.4.1). Phase 12a's 13.3 was chosen when the host ran 13.3; Phase 13 valued the 13.3-vs-13.4 difference only as a way to tell estate nvcc from host nvcc in run.do_compile, which the sysroot PATH shows just as well. Production recipes take nvcc/headers/libraries ONLY from the recipe's sysroot (DEPENDS cuda-toolkit-bin-native / cuda-toolkit-bin), never from /usr/local/cuda-*; libcuda.so and libnvidia-ml.so.1 stay host-driver-provided (S2). The toolkit, cuDNN and driver are BINARY_EXTERNAL under NVIDIA's EULA/SLA - no source-built claim is made for them. Recipe path: meta-symoneural/recipes-cuda/cuda-toolkit-bin/ from NVIDIA's public local installer with installer + EULA sha256 recorded and the EULA text under meta-symoneural/files/custom-licenses/. Not yet written: the installer has not been fetched.
